D1.name: Hiring Readiness Optimization
D1.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the core DS technical stack comprehensively across 6 months — Pandas, SQL, stats, supervised/unsupervised ML, deep learning, NLP, and a Flask deployment — but interview prep is largely deferred to Month 6 with only a brief mention of LeetCode and mock interviews. Portfolio work is solid with two capstone projects but lacks cloud deployment or MLOps integration, which are increasingly expected globally. Plan 2 integrates interview prep from Month 1 with weekly coding challenge goals, behavioral prep, and ML concept articulation practice, distributed across all 6 months. Plan 2's capstone is a single evolving end-to-end project that culminates in cloud deployment (AWS SageMaker), Docker containerization, an interactive dashboard, and an MLOps pipeline — significantly more employer-worthy for a global DS role. Plan 2 also explicitly covers system design for ML, which is a differentiator at FAANG-level hiring.
D1.winner_reason: Plan 2 distributes interview prep throughout all 6 months, builds a production-deployed capstone with MLOps and cloud components, and explicitly addresses system design — all materially increasing hiring readiness over Plan 1's back-loaded approach.

core_technical_readiness.justification: Covers the full DS stack including Pandas, SQL, stats, ML algorithms, deep learning, NLP, and basic Flask deployment. Misses cloud deployment, Docker, and MLOps which are increasingly expected globally for DS roles.

interview_prep_readiness.justification: Interview prep is almost entirely deferred to Month 6 (Weeks 23-24). LeetCode and mock interviews are mentioned but not systematically scheduled. No ML system design or case study practice is included throughout the plan.

D2.name: Time-Constrained Feasibility
D2.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 does not explicitly calculate total hours or provide a time budget, making it impossible to verify hour compliance. The weekly content is dense — for example, Week 12 covers XGBoost, LightGBM, SVMs, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning in a single week at 2 hours/day (14 hours), which is ambitious. Plan 2 explicitly calculates 255 planned hours against 288 available hours with a 33-hour buffer, demonstrating deliberate time management. Plan 2's monthly hour budgets (~42-43 hours) align with 2 hours/day over ~21 working days. However, Plan 2 also has ambitious weeks — Month 5 covering AWS setup, SageMaker deployment, Docker, and PySpark in 4 weeks at 2 hours/day is a heavy cognitive load. Both plans have some overengineering risk, but Plan 2's explicit hour tracking and buffer make it more defensible.
D2.winner_reason: Plan 2 explicitly tracks total hours, planned hours, and buffer hours, demonstrating deliberate feasibility planning that Plan 1 entirely lacks.

hour_compliance.justification: No explicit hour calculation or budget provided. At 2 hours/day over 6 months (~360 hours total), the plan likely fits, but there is no verification or buffer planning, making compliance unverifiable.

cognitive_load_realism.justification: Most weeks are manageable but some are dense — Week 12 packs XGBoost, LightGBM, SVMs, cross-validation, and hyperparameter tuning into 14 hours. Week 19 covers NLP fundamentals, text preprocessing, word embeddings, and sentiment analysis simultaneously.

overengineering_avoidance.justification: Mostly appropriate for the role and timeline. Advanced CNN architectures (ResNet, Inception) and RNNs in Month 5 are somewhat ambitious for 2 hours/day but are relevant to DS. Flask deployment is appropriately scoped.

hour_compliance.justification: Explicitly calculates 288 total available hours, 255 planned hours, and 33 buffer hours. Monthly budgets of 42-43 hours align precisely with 2 hours/day. This is the most rigorous hour planning of the two plans.

D4.comparative_analysis: Plan 1 covers the standard global DS skill set — Python, SQL, statistics, scikit-learn, XGBoost, deep learning, NLP, and basic deployment. This is solid but represents the baseline expectation for DS roles globally. It does not include cloud platforms, MLOps tooling, or modern NLP (Transformers/Hugging Face), which are increasingly demanded by global employers. Plan 2 goes significantly further by including AWS SageMaker, Docker, MLOps principles, PySpark, Hugging Face Transformers, and interactive dashboards — all of which are in high demand globally for DS roles at innovative companies. The inclusion of Transformers and cloud deployment in particular reflects the current state of the global DS job market, where production ML skills differentiate candidates.
D4.winner_reason: Plan 2 includes cloud deployment, MLOps, Transformers, and PySpark — emerging and advanced tools that are genuinely in demand globally and differentiate candidates beyond the baseline DS skill set covered by Plan 1.
